rejected_candidates.reason: It is the paper's general summation framework rather than the selected Cholesky conclusion. The protected-tree instances needed by Theorem 4.4 remain part of the paper-specific execution model.
Its division case feeds Lemma 4.1 and its square-root case feeds Lemma 4.3; the selected tasks retain the stronger factorization consequences.
The specialized recursive-summation estimate is interesting but less central to the paper's LU and Cholesky contribution than the selected application ladder.
The paper says it follows immediately from Lemma 4.1 and presents it as an improvement of a delegated textbook theorem; the LU and Cholesky targets are more central.
It is an immediate specialization of Corollary 3.2; its coefficient is used in Theorem 4.4, which is selected instead.
They are described as obtained by directly modifying textbook proofs, retain quadratic terms, and are not stated as named finite results.
They justify limitations of simpler rounding models but are not as representative as the paper's main backward-error results.

T1.decision: Skipped after a fresh complete-paper reread and frozen-source comparison. Every improved nu or (n+1)u result depends on the paper's protected-summation argument, which NumStability does not contain. Its conventional LU and Cholesky theorems prove the older gamma bounds and cannot derive the sharper unconditional constants; the only nearby residual-to-coefficient assembly result is short and does not materially reduce the protected-tree proof.

T2.decision: Skipped after a fresh complete-paper reread and frozen-source comparison. Theorem 4.2 and Theorem 4.4 reuse the same missing protected-summation result and add only short triangular-support and perturbation assemblies; they do not expose two independent substantial NumStability results. The triangular-solve results invoked later are textbook results adapted without a new named proof target in this paper.

T3.decision: Use all of Theorem 4.4: the conventional Cholesky execution, local estimates (4.5), exact backward relation, and full diag((i+1)u) and (n+1)u bounds.

selection_policy: Use a finite claim made and proved in this paper.
Reject experiments, vague asymptotics, and claims whose proof is mainly delegated elsewhere.
Prefer exact displayed bounds and identities.
Keep the fixed Lean setting condition-neutral and paper-scoped.
Assign tiers only after verified frozen-library searches.
